_why: @capacitor/haptics was missing for weeks and NOTHING could notice. js/haptics.js asks
for window.Capacitor.Plugins.Haptics, gets null on a native build, falls through to
navigator.vibrate?.() which does not exist in an iOS WKWebView, inside a try/catch that
swallows. Silence. And the file's own comment says iOS staying silent is 'correct rather
than fake', so the INTENDED silence hid the UNINTENDED one.
This file is the declared list of what the shell must provide. tests/unit.test.js checks
it BOTH ways: every entry here must really be wired up, and every Capacitor.Plugins.X the
web code asks for must appear here. The reverse direction is the one that catches the
haptics class, because that plugin was referenced everywhere and declared nowhere.
_declared_two_ways: npm plugins need FOUR places, and npm alone is not enough:
3 and 4 are generated by `npx cap sync`: verify them, never hand-edit them.
local plugins have no npm entry at all. They are source files that must exist, be in the
Xcode target, and be REGISTERED per platform. Capacitor 8 does not auto-discover a plugin
living in the app target, which is exactly how BhVault shipped compiled-but-unregistered
on iOS while working on Android.

plugins.degrades: no resume/pause events and no shell version in Settings
no reminders; the app still runs
every tap, payout and impact is silent on native, and nothing errors
plugins.known_gap: NOT INSTALLED. This is the defect that motivated the manifest, left in place deliberately so the guard has a live example. Adding the dep needs `npx cap sync` plus an iOS and an Android rebuild and store upload, which is the native lane, not the test lane. Remove this field in the same commit that adds the dependency; the guard FAILS if the flag is still here once it is really installed.

plugins.degrades: no steps, active energy or workouts; the game loses its main input

identity stops surviving a reinstall, so a returning player mints a NEW EMPTY account instead of recovering. js/social.js reads a missing plugin as an empty vault ON PURPOSE, because that is right for browsers, which is why this failed silently on iOS for weeks.
